data.narrative:
Spaceium is a Seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by orbital mechanics and propulsion specialists with relevant NASA and legacy engine experience. The company has raised $6.3M to date. The comparable universe comprises five public Space & Aerospace companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and eight private peers including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, though no narrow peer set exists at identical stage and valuation tier.

A single applicable valuation method supports this analysis: Stage-Progression anchoring. Using total capital raised ($6.3M) as a proxy for post-Seed value, a 2.5x step-up multiplier—standard for Seed to next-stage progression—yields $15.75M. This represents the median point in a triangulated range of $13M to $18M, bounded by ±15% sensitivity around the 2.5x multiplier.

The Peer-Median approach was not applicable; while 11 same-sector peers exist, filtering for stage, timing, and valuation tier yielded insufficient datapoints. Public-Comp Anchoring could not be applied as target revenue is not disclosed. The single-method constraint and lack of revenue data represent material uncertainties. The $13M–$18M range is supported only by stage-progression mechanics and should be stress-tested against future revenue visibility and technology risk assessment as the company matures.
